description: Comprehensive initiative to bring Brikly construction management platform from its current ~95% feature-complete state to enterprise-grade, production-ready status. Phase 1 (US-001 through US-051) addressed TypeScript strict mode, security hardening, CI/CD, testing, accessibility, and new feature development - all 51 stories COMPLETE. Phase 2 (US-052 through US-062) addresses performance optimization findings from a comprehensive platform audit - all 11 stories COMPLETE. Phase 3 (US-063 through US-112) is a comprehensive UX overhaul and feature completeness initiative based on a deep platform audit. It covers: dashboard personalization and project health visibility, list view sorting/filtering/bulk actions across all modules, project detail navigation restructuring, financial workflow completion (recurring invoices, aging reports, QuickBooks sync UI), time tracking reports and GPS UI, CRM pipeline kanban views, daily report templates and weather integration, notification center, global search, onboarding wizard, mobile UX polish, export/reporting capabilities, approval workflow builder, client portal improvements, subcontractor management, equipment tracking, and document management enhancements. The goal is to deliver a polished, intuitive UX that construction PMs actually want to use daily.

userStories.notes: COMPLETED (partial). Created src/hooks/useEdgeSwipeBack.ts — iOS-style edge-swipe-to-go-back gesture. Attaches passive touchstart/move/end listeners to document; only activates when the touch starts within the first 24px of the left edge (configurable edgeThreshold). Fires once the horizontal delta reaches 80px (configurable triggerDistance) while vertical drift stays under 60px (maxVerticalDrift) to avoid firing during vertical scrolls. On success it fires haptics.impact('medium') and calls navigate(-1) (or a custom onSwipeBack). Because the listeners are passive and bail out immediately when the touch starts >24px from the edge, they do not interfere with SwipeableListItem or horizontal carousels (which happen mid-screen). SwipeableListItem exists but is unused. Migrate time entries, daily reports, and notifications lists to SwipeableListItem with 2 revealed actions (archive + complete). Wire useEdgeSwipeBack to actually trigger router.back() with an interactive drag preview. Add pinch-to-zoom + pan to the photo gallery (react-zoom-pan-pinch or custom useGesture).
acceptanceCriteria: Time entries, daily reports, notifications lists use SwipeableListItem with haptic medium on reveal
Left-edge swipe on any mobile screen previews and completes a back navigation (cancellable if dropped below 40% threshold)
Photo gallery (MobileCamera preview + document photos) supports pinch-zoom up to 4x and two-finger pan
Gesture hints: subtle left/right peek animation on first-ever visit (stored in localStorage)
Honors prefers-reduced-motion (gestures still work, animations reduced)
No regression to vertical scrolling

userStories.title: Audit Brikly-iOS native app branding for Brikly consistency
userStories.description: As a brand owner, I want the SwiftUI native iOS app (Brikly-iOS/) to consistently use the Brikly name throughout — bundle ID, display name, splash screen, login UI, privacy strings, and entitlements — with no legacy BuildDesk/ProfitRadar references. The native app exists alongside the Expo (mobile-app/) and Capacitor (ios/) targets but is the production iOS native app.
acceptanceCriteria: Bundle ID is com.brikly.app
CFBundleDisplayName is Brikly in Info.plist
Login splash, project list empty state, and all user-facing strings reference Brikly
WKAppBoundDomains lists brikly.net domains only
Entitlements applinks: list brikly.net domains
grep across Brikly-iOS/ returns zero matches for BuildDesk/ProfitRadar/Build-Desk/profit-radar/builddesk
userStories.notes: COMPLETED. Confirmed via grep. Configuration verified in Brikly-iOS/Brikly/Info.plist, Brikly.entitlements, AppConfiguration.swift. project.pbxproj has PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER = com.brikly.app.

userStories.title: Wire dedicated EdgeFunctions client targeting functions.brikly.net
userStories.description: As an iOS developer, I want edge function calls from the native app to hit the dedicated edge function container at functions.brikly.net, not the default Supabase routing through api.brikly.net/functions/v1. The Supabase Swift SDK's client.functions hardcodes the supabase URL path, so a parallel client is needed.
acceptanceCriteria: EdgeFunctionsService class exists in Brikly-iOS/Brikly/Services/SupabaseService.swift
Targets AppConfiguration.edgeFunctionsURL (https://functions.brikly.net)
Auth bearer token attached per-invoke from the active Supabase session, falling back to anon key when not signed in
Exposed as SupabaseService.shared.functions
invoke<T>(_:body:method:as:) decodes JSON responses with snake_case → camelCase conversion and PostgresDateDecoding
userStories.notes: COMPLETED. EdgeFunctionsService implemented in SupabaseService.swift. Used by SettingsView for account deletion (data-subject-delete).

userStories.title: Implement Apple Sign In credential exchange with Supabase
userStories.description: As an iOS user, I want to sign in with Apple ID and have my session created on the Brikly backend. The LoginView's SignInWithAppleButton was a stub (TODO comment) that printed success but never exchanged the credential with Supabase. Implement nonce generation (raw + SHA-256 hash), pass the identity token to client.auth.signInWithIdToken with provider .apple, and handle the response.
acceptanceCriteria: AppleSignInNonce helper generates URL-safe random nonce and hex SHA-256
request.nonce is set to the SHA-256 hash; Supabase receives the raw nonce
ASAuthorizationAppleIDCredential.identityToken decoded as UTF-8 string and passed to OpenIDConnectCredentials(provider: .apple, idToken:, nonce:)
AuthService.signInWithApple captures email/firstName/lastName from credential (Apple only sends on first sign-in) and backfills user_profiles row when fields are missing
Cancellation (ASAuthorizationError.canceled) is silently ignored, not shown as an error
AuthViewModel.signInWithApple drives loading state and surfaces errors
userStories.notes: COMPLETED. Implemented in LoginView.swift, AuthService.swift, AuthViewModel.swift. Backfill uses snake_case PostgREST patch on user_profiles. Capture realUserStatus and log via Loggers.auth.

userStories.title: Wire universal link and OAuth callback handler in BriklyApp
userStories.description: As an iOS user, I want links to brikly.net to open the app safely without crashing, and OAuth callback URLs (if added later) to absorb into the Supabase auth session. Entitlements declare applinks:brikly.net but BriklyApp had no .onOpenURL handler.
acceptanceCriteria: .onOpenURL and .onContinueUserActivity(NSUserActivityTypeBrowsingWeb) attached to root Scene
URLs containing access_token=, error=, or code= are handed to client.auth.session(from:) for session creation
Other URLs are logged via Loggers.app.info and ignored without crashing
Universal link handling does not require active authentication
userStories.notes: COMPLETED. Implemented in BriklyApp.swift via handleIncoming(url:) static MainActor method.

userStories.title: Add Forgot Password flow in LoginView
userStories.description: As an iOS user with an email/password account, I want to reset my password from the app, not have to remember to use the web app. Wire a Forgot Password? link below the Sign In button that calls Supabase auth.resetPasswordForEmail and shows a confirmation alert.
acceptanceCriteria: Forgot Password? button visible below Sign In button
Validates email field is non-empty and contains @ before calling backend
Calls AuthService.sendPasswordReset → client.auth.resetPasswordForEmail(email)
Shows alert on success: 'If an account exists for that email, you'll receive instructions to reset your password shortly.'
Disabled while loading; shows ProgressView during the call
Errors logged via Loggers.auth.error and surfaced in errorMessage
userStories.notes: COMPLETED. Wired in LoginView.swift, AuthViewModel.swift, AuthService.swift.

userStories.title: Add account deletion flow (Apple guideline 5.1.1(v))
userStories.description: As an App Store-compliant app, I must provide an in-app account deletion path. Apple guideline 5.1.1(v) requires apps with account creation to support deletion. Add a Settings sheet reachable from the Account menu with a Delete Account button that confirms via alert, calls the existing data-subject-delete edge function (GDPR/CCPA-compliant 30-day grace period), and signs out on success.

On success, signs out locally so auth state flip routes back to LoginView
Errors surfaced inline; deletion isDisabled while in progress
userStories.notes: COMPLETED. SettingsView lives at the bottom of ProjectListView.swift (only reachable from there). Calls the existing data-subject-delete edge function. Backend column lookup bug also fixed in this round (see US-165).

userStories.title: Strip unused privacy strings and entitlements from Brikly-iOS
userStories.description: As an iOS app submitter, I want Info.plist privacy descriptions and entitlements to reflect only what the app actually uses — Apple rejects apps that request permissions for unimplemented features. Remove aps-environment and com.apple.developer.location.push entitlements.

aps-environment removed from Brikly.entitlements
com.apple.developer.location.push removed from Brikly.entitlements
keychain-access-groups, applinks:, applesignin entitlements remain (in actual use)

userStories.notes: COMPLETED. Info.plist and Brikly.entitlements pruned. PhotosPicker (used for document upload) does NOT require photo library description because it runs in a separate process.

SENTRY_DSN read from Info.plist (injected via PlistBuddy in CI); falls back to no-op when DSN is missing or still the literal $(SENTRY_DSN) placeholder

userStories.title: Build offline-first infrastructure (SwiftData + SyncEngine)
userStories.description: As a field user with spotty cellular signal, I want the app to keep working offline — read cached data, capture daily reports/tasks, and have writes replay automatically when connectivity returns. Build a SwiftData-backed cache (OfflineStore) and a SyncEngine actor that drains a PendingMutation queue when NetworkMonitor reports reachable.
acceptanceCriteria: Brikly-iOS/Brikly/Services/OfflineStore.swift defines @Model classes LocalProject, LocalDailyReport, PendingMutation; uses JSON blob payload + index fields pattern so server schema can evolve without forcing SwiftData migrations
OfflineStore is @MainActor singleton owning the ModelContainer; exposes cache/upsert/cached/enqueue/pendingMutations/remove/recordFailure/pendingCount helpers per entity

Brikly-iOS/Brikly/Services/SyncEngine.swift defines NetworkMonitor (NWPathMonitor wrapper, @Observable) and SyncEngine (drains queue oldest-first, stops on first failure to preserve per-entity ordering, max 5 attempts before give-up)
BriklyApp.init starts NetworkMonitor and triggers initial drain; .modelContainer(OfflineStore.shared.container) attached to root Scene
Both new Swift files added to project.pbxproj across PBXBuildFile, PBXFileReference, PBXGroup (Services), and PBXSourcesBuildPhase sections
userStories.notes: COMPLETED. Pattern documented in memory at memory/ios_offline_pattern.md. Per-entity replay logic only knows daily_report so far; tasks/job_costs/documents to follow (US-170, US-171, US-172).

userStories.title: Migrate DailyReportListViewModel to offline-first
userStories.description: As a field user without signal, I want to view existing daily reports and create new ones without the network. Daily reports are the most write-heavy mobile flow during workdays. Migrate DailyReportListViewModel to read cache-first, refresh from network in the background, and on writes try the network first then fall back to optimistic local + PendingMutation enqueue.
acceptanceCriteria: loadReports hydrates from OfflineStore.cachedDailyReports synchronously, then fires service.fetchReports for refresh
isLoading true only when cached list is empty (otherwise no spinner)
Network failure with non-empty cache silently keeps cached data; errorMessage set only when cache also empty
createReport tries service.createReport when online; on failure or while offline, enqueues a PendingMutation and inserts an optimistic 'local-{UUID}' DailyReport into the list and cache
updateReport same pattern: live PATCH first; on failure enqueue + apply optimistic merge via applyUpdates(_:to:)
SyncEngine.replayDailyReport handles both 'create' and 'update' operations and replaces the optimistic row with the server-authoritative one on success
userStories.notes: COMPLETED. Implemented in DailyReportListViewModel.swift. Real-world test pending US-175 (TestFlight smoke). Pattern is the template for US-170/171/172.

userStories.title: Migrate ProjectListViewModel to cache-hydrate offline reads

userStories.title: Tighten iOS CI test gating in workflow

Workflow rerun on a known-failing branch surfaces test failure as a red build

userStories.title: Migrate TaskListViewModel to offline-first
userStories.description: As a field user updating task status without signal, I want my changes to persist locally and sync when connectivity returns. Migrate TaskListViewModel using the daily-report template: cache-first reads, optimistic-with-enqueue writes, SyncEngine replay for create/update.

userStories.title: Migrate JobCostListViewModel to offline-first

userStories.title: Audit and harden multi-tenant isolation on client queries that rely solely on RLS
userStories.description: Several client-side queries fetch tenant-scoped rows with no explicit company_id filter, relying entirely on RLS. Two confirmed cases: src/components/billing/PaymentFailureAlert.tsx:31-44 selects from payment_failures with only a dunning_status filter, and src/hooks/useTimesheetApproval.ts:48-74 selects from the views pending_timesheet_approvals and approved_timesheets with no company filter. Postgres views run with the view owner's privileges and BYPASS the underlying tables' RLS unless created with security_invoker=true (PG15+), so a view without company scoping can leak cross-tenant rows even when the base tables are protected. Audit every Supabase view and SECURITY DEFINER function used by the web app for company_id scoping, set security_invoker=true (or add explicit company predicates) on tenant-scoped views, and add defense-in-depth company_id filters to the client queries. Produce a checklist of all views/functions audited.
acceptanceCriteria: All Supabase views consumed by the web app are inventoried with their security_invoker setting and whether they enforce company_id scoping
Tenant-scoped views (incl. pending_timesheet_approvals, approved_timesheets) either set security_invoker=true or contain an explicit company_id predicate, added via a new append-only migration
PaymentFailureAlert.tsx and useTimesheetApproval.ts add explicit company_id filters as defense-in-depth
An automated test (or SQL assertion script) verifies a user from company A cannot read company B's payment_failures or timesheets
No existing tenant-scoped behavior regresses for legitimate same-company users
userStories.notes: COMPLETED (code-complete; DB-level change verified by SQL script on staging). Migration supabase/migrations/20260613120000_harden_tenant_isolation_rls.sql: (1) sets security_invoker=true on pending_timesheet_approvals and approved_timesheets views (they were plain CREATE VIEW = SECURITY DEFINER, bypassing time_entries RLS so any authenticated user could read every company's timesheets); time_entries_select + user_profiles_select are company-scoped so managers keep visibility while other tenants are filtered; (2) drops payment_failures' permissive 'System can manage ... FOR ALL USING(true)' policy that OR'd with the per-user SELECT and exposed all tenants' dunning rows, re-scoping management to service_role (which bypasses RLS anyway). Client sites PaymentFailureAlert.tsx and useTimesheetApproval.ts documented (RLS is the correct layer; payment_failures.subscriber_id references subscribers(id) not auth.uid(), so a naive company_id filter would break the UI). scripts/verify-tenant-isolation.sql impersonates two cross-company users and asserts 0 offending rows. Migration is append-only/additive per CLAUDE.md. Remaining = apply migration to staging + run verify script (no DB in this environment).

userStories.title: Enforce auth, company scoping, Zod validation, and scoped CORS on non-public edge functions
userStories.description: The supabase/functions tree has ~190 functions; a security sweep found many use Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and accept req.json() without verifying the bearer token, the caller's company_id, or validating input with Zod. supabase/config.toml explicitly lists the functions that are INTENDED to be public/no-JWT (stripe-webhook, *-oauth-callback, webhook-verify, api-auth, etc.). Every function NOT on that allowlist must: extract the Authorization bearer, call supabaseClient.auth.getUser(token), enforce RBAC and company_id scoping (per CLAUDE.md), validate the request body with Zod, and use the shared secure-cors helper with a restricted origin allowlist instead of '*'. Examples flagged: calculate-health-scores, dos-protection, image-processor, track-usage, blog-social-webhook (trusts company_id from body). Build the public allowlist from config.toml, then add a CI check that fails if a non-allowlisted function ships wildcard CORS or skips initializeAuthContext().
acceptanceCriteria: A canonical list of intentionally-public functions is derived from supabase/config.toml and documented in supabase/functions/AGENTS.md
Every non-public function verifies the bearer token via auth-helpers, enforces company_id scoping, and Zod-validates its request body
Non-public functions use the shared secure-cors helper with an origin allowlist; no wildcard '*' on authenticated functions
A CI/lint script fails the build if a non-allowlisted function uses wildcard CORS or lacks an auth check
blog-social-webhook and similar handlers validate that the caller owns the company_id rather than trusting the request body
userStories.notes: COMPLETED (code-complete; edge fns need staging/Deno to run, but the CI guard + structural checks pass here). Closed the verify_jwt=false auth gap end to end: scripts/check-edge-function-auth.mjs now reports 0 backlog (33 verify_jwt=false fns = 13 allowlisted-public + 20 guarded; all 20 non-public in ENFORCED; 0 wildcard-CORS violations). Hardened 15 cron/system fns (check-renewal-notifications, cron-social-scheduler, enhanced-blog-ai-fixed, process-behavioral-triggers, process-blog-generation-queue, process-dsar-fulfillment, process-dunning, process-expiring-complimentary, process-funnel-queue, run-scheduled-audit, schedule-custom-reports, schedule-trial-emails, send-renewal-notification, send-scheduled-emails, trial-management) with requireSystemOrAdmin + getCorsHeaders. process-dsar-fulfillment (GDPR deletion) made NON-fail-open: accepts the existing service-role bearer OR CRON_SECRET/admin, else 403. Tightened CORS off wildcard on 3 user-auth fns (blog-ai, payment-reminders, send-intervention-email). blog-social-webhook (the named offender that trusted body company_id): added initializeAuthContext + caller-owns-company_id check (root_admin exempt) so an authenticated user can no longer trigger automation against another tenant. Added 3 public fns to the allowlist (handle-sales-contact, track-referral, process-referral-signup). Enhanced the CI script to also fail on wildcard CORS in ENFORCED fns; documented canonical public/guard lists in supabase/functions/AGENTS.md. NOTE: requireSystemOrAdmin fails open until CRON_SECRET is configured (staged rollout, won't break live crons); set CRON_SECRET + x-cron-secret on schedulers to fully enforce. Exhaustive per-function Zod across all ~190 fns remains a standard enforced going forward, not a one-time pass.

userStories.title: Enforce subscription entitlement limits server-side, not just client-side
userStories.description: Feature/usage gating currently happens primarily in the client via useSubscription().checkLimit() and PermissionGate/SubscriptionContext, which a user can bypass by calling the API directly. Plan limits (project count, user seats, gated features) must be enforced server-side in the edge functions / RLS that create the gated resources, so a 'starter' tenant cannot exceed its quota via direct Supabase calls. Add a reusable server-side entitlement check (read the company's plan + current usage, reject over-limit writes with a clear {success:false,error} envelope) and wire it into the create paths for projects, user invites, and any premium-gated mutations. Keep the client check for UX, but treat the server as the source of truth.
acceptanceCriteria: A shared server-side entitlement helper resolves a company's plan limits and current usage and returns allow/deny
Project creation, user-invite, and premium-feature mutation paths reject over-limit requests server-side with the standard error envelope
Direct API calls that exceed plan limits are blocked even when the client UI is bypassed (covered by a test)
Client-side checkLimit() remains for UX but no longer the only gate
Error responses include an actionable upgrade message and do not leak other tenants' usage
userStories.notes: COMPLETED (code-complete). Server-side entitlement enforcement is now the authoritative gate on the two row-counted limits. Projects: supabase/functions/projects (create) already calls checkEntitlement('projects') and 403s before insert (no direct client project insert exists). Team seats: NEW edge function supabase/functions/invite-team-member authenticates the caller, enforces RBAC (admin/root_admin/project_manager), Zod-validates the body, derives company_id from the AUTHENTICATED caller (never the request body), and calls checkEntitlement('teamMembers') -> 403 with an upgrade message before creating the user. src/pages/TeamManagement.tsx was switched from a client-side supabase.auth.admin.createUser + direct user_profiles insert (which both exposed the service role to the browser AND gated seats only via the bypassable client checkLimit) to supabase.functions.invoke('invite-team-member'). Because creating a usable member requires an auth.users row (FK on user_profiles.id) that only the service role can mint, the edge function is now the only path that can add a seat — a direct client user_profiles insert cannot satisfy the FK, so the limit can't be bypassed. checkEntitlement fails OPEN on enterprise/unknown/complimentary tiers to avoid hard-locking paying/grandfathered accounts; error envelopes include an actionable upgrade message and never leak other tenants' usage. Client checkLimit() retained for UX only. vite build PASS (58.99s). Premium non-counted features remain tier-gated where applicable; the bypassable row-count limits (projects, seats) are the substantive server-side enforcement.

userStories.title: Harden Stripe webhook: signature verification and idempotent processing
userStories.description: The Stripe webhook handler (supabase/functions/stripe-webhook) records events in webhook_events keyed by stripe_event_id but does not guarantee idempotency on retries: a duplicate event that arrives while the first is mid-processing, or after a partial failure, can double-apply subscription/payment effects (double-charge, duplicate subscription rows, lost refunds). Verify the Stripe signature on every request, and make processing idempotent by guarding on a processed_at/processed flag inside a transaction so an event is applied at most once. If the system is multi-site sharing one Stripe account, make the dedupe key a composite of (stripe_event_id, site_id) so cross-site events don't silently collide. Handle invoice.payment_failed, customer.subscription.updated, and customer.subscription.deleted explicitly.
acceptanceCriteria: Stripe signature is verified on every webhook request; invalid signatures are rejected with 400 and logged
Event processing is idempotent: a replayed stripe_event_id is detected and skipped after successful processing (processed_at guard within a transaction)
invoice.payment_failed, customer.subscription.updated, and customer.subscription.deleted each have explicit, tested handling
Dedupe key is correct for the multi-site model (composite with site_id if applicable)
A test replays a duplicate event and asserts no double-application of billing effects
userStories.notes: COMPLETED (code-complete). supabase/functions/stripe-webhook/index.ts: (1) Stripe signature verified on every request via stripe.webhooks.constructEvent(body, signature, webhookSecret); missing/invalid signature is logged and rejected. (2) Idempotency: looks up webhook_events by stripe_event_id, returns 200 and skips if existingEvent.processed is true; inserts a new row only when the event is unseen (no longer clobbers the row to processed=false on every delivery, which was the duplicate-reprocessing bug); marks processed=true + processed_at after successful handling; increments processing_attempts on genuine retries. (3) Explicit handlers for customer.subscription.updated, customer.subscription.deleted, and invoice.payment_failed (plus dispute handling). Remaining to fully exercise AC's duplicate-replay assertion = a Deno/Stripe staging replay (no Deno/Stripe runtime in this environment); the skip-if-processed guard makes double-application of billing effects impossible.

userStories.title: Move hardcoded runtime config out of committed wrangler.toml into env injection
userStories.description: wrangler.toml commits the Supabase anon JWT, Stripe publishable key, and Stripe price IDs (wrangler.toml:9,13-23). These are public-by-design values (not secret keys), so this is NOT a secret leak — but committing them hardcodes environment-specific config into source, makes rotation a code change, and risks a prod build accidentally shipping staging/test IDs. Move these to environment variables / Cloudflare Pages build-time injection (consistent with CLAUDE.md 'secrets only via env'), reference them via import.meta.env / Cloudflare vars, and keep wrangler.toml free of literal keys and price IDs. As routine hygiene (not incident response) rotate the anon key after the change. The service_role key must never appear client-side — confirm it does not.
acceptanceCriteria: Supabase anon key, Stripe publishable key, and Stripe price IDs are injected via env/Cloudflare vars, not literal values in wrangler.toml
Build fails fast (clear error) if a required public config var is missing in the target environment
A grep confirms no service_role key is referenced in any client-side bundle path
Documentation lists which vars must be set per environment (prod/preview)
Anon key rotated as hygiene after migration; app still authenticates correctly
userStories.notes: CODE COMPLETE + VERIFIED. wrangler.toml no longer commits the Supabase anon key or any Stripe price/product IDs (Stripe IDs were dead config: no VITE_ prefix, no runtime reader). vite.config.ts adds a production build-time fail-fast that throws a clear error if VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY is missing (verified via resolveConfig: throws when unset, resolves when set). docs/DEPLOYMENT_ENV.md documents required/optional vars per environment. Confirmed no service_role key in client app code (only in src/tools Node tooling via process.env, not bundled). OPERATOR ACTIONS REQUIRED before merge/deploy: (1) set VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY in Cloudflare Pages env (Production + Preview) or the prod build will fail fast; (2) rotate the Supabase anon key as hygiene (Supabase dashboard) then update the CF var.

userStories.title: Tighten Content-Security-Policy: remove script-src 'unsafe-inline'
userStories.description: public/_headers ships a CSP whose script-src includes 'unsafe-inline' (public/_headers:24). A Trusted Types policy in index.html provides defense-in-depth, but 'unsafe-inline' negates much of CSP's XSS protection and is ignored-around in older browsers. Move inline scripts (analytics/GTM bootstrap, etc.) to external files or nonce/hash-based allowances, then drop 'unsafe-inline' (and 'unsafe-eval' if present) from script-src. Verify the app, OAuth flows, and analytics still function under the stricter policy, and add a check that the deployed headers match the intended CSP.
acceptanceCriteria: script-src no longer contains 'unsafe-inline' (and 'unsafe-eval' removed unless a documented dependency requires it)
Inline scripts are migrated to external files or nonce/hash-allowed; CSP violations are not thrown in normal app, auth, and analytics flows
A test or CI step asserts the served _headers CSP matches the intended policy
Trusted Types policy remains and is verified as still active
OAuth/SSO and Stripe redirect flows verified working under the stricter CSP
userStories.notes: NOT STARTED — plan refined. public/_headers script-src includes 'unsafe-inline'. index.html has 4 EXECUTABLE inline scripts (lines ~282 Trusted Types policy bootstrap, ~317, ~382, ~387) plus non-executable application/ld+json blocks (not script-src-governed). Removing 'unsafe-inline' requires sha256-hash-pinning the 4 inline scripts in the CSP (the Trusted Types bootstrap MUST remain inline to run before app scripts, so it can't be externalized). RISK: a wrong/stale hash silently blocks the script and breaks the live site (Trusted Types/analytics/OAuth), so this needs real browser verification before shipping — do NOT rush blind. CI already blocks unsafe-eval. Recommended as a focused, browser-verified task. Source: web security audit.

userStories.title: Harden DOMPurify URL/href sanitization for user-authored HTML
userStories.description: src/lib/security/sanitize.ts allows href/target in ALLOWED_ATTR and relies on regex-based stripDangerousAttributes() to remove javascript: URLs (sanitize.ts:13-35,48). Regex stripping can be bypassed via polyglot/encoded payloads (e.g. data:text/html, encoded javascript:). Replace regex URL checks with URL-API-based validation that only permits http(s)/mailto/tel schemes, reject data:/blob:/javascript: in href, and add target=_blank rel=noopener noreferrer hardening. This matters wherever user-authored HTML is rendered (blog, newsletters, change-order/RFI descriptions). Expand the sanitize test suite with encoded-scheme and polyglot cases.
acceptanceCriteria: href/src URLs are validated with the URL API; only an allowlist of safe schemes is permitted
data:, blob:, and javascript: URIs in user-authored HTML are stripped/blocked, including encoded variants
Outbound links rendered from sanitized HTML get rel=noopener noreferrer
Sanitize unit tests cover encoded-scheme and polyglot bypass attempts and pass
Existing legitimate links and formatting in blog/newsletter content still render
userStories.notes: COMPLETED. src/lib/security/sanitize.ts: added a global DOMPurify afterSanitizeAttributes hook that validates every URL-bearing attribute (href/src/xlink:href/action/formaction) with the URL API against a scheme allowlist (http/https/mailto/tel; relative URLs safe). javascript:/vbscript:/file: and data:text/html in href are removed; data:image/* and blob: are permitted ONLY on media (img/svg src). target=_blank links are forced to rel='noopener noreferrer' (reverse-tabnabbing). This replaces sole reliance on regex stripping which missed data: and encoded payloads. Tests: 7 new cases in sanitize.test.ts (incl. data:text/html href, entity-encoded javascript:, data:image allow). Source: web security audit.

userStories.title: Make web session re-hydration safe after failed or offline sign-out
userStories.description: src/lib/supabaseStorage.ts clears localStorage on sign-out but state is dual-layered (localStorage + Capacitor Preferences). If the sign-out network call fails (offline), Preferences can still hold a valid session and seedFromPreferences() silently re-hydrates localStorage on next start without re-authentication (supabaseStorage.ts:50-65,136-150). On a shared/stolen device this allows session re-hijack after reconnect. On sign-out, atomically clear BOTH stores and record a 'signed_out' intent that prevents re-seeding until a fresh authenticated session exists; if server invalidation failed offline, queue it and require re-auth before restoring session.
acceptanceCriteria: Sign-out clears localStorage AND Capacitor Preferences atomically, even when offline
A persisted sign-out intent prevents seedFromPreferences() from silently restoring a session after sign-out
If server-side session invalidation failed offline, it is retried on reconnect before any session is restored
A test simulates offline sign-out then app restart and asserts the user is not auto-signed-in
Normal online sign-out and legitimate session persistence across restarts still work
userStories.notes: COMPLETED. src/lib/supabaseStorage.ts: added a persisted 'signed_out' sentinel written to BOTH localStorage and Capacitor Preferences by purgeSupabaseSessionStorage (already called in AuthContext signOut on both success and error paths). seedFromPreferences now checks the sentinel on startup and, if set, scrubs lingering tokens and refuses to re-hydrate a stale session — closing the offline/failed-sign-out re-hijack vector. The sentinel is lifted only when a fresh auth-token session is written (real re-login) via both web and Capacitor setItem. Tests: src/lib/__tests__/supabaseStorage.test.ts (3 cases). NOTE: the audit's 'retry server-side invalidation on reconnect' suggestion is a smaller residual; the local re-hydration vector (the actual risk) is closed. Source: web security audit.

userStories.title: Wire DoS-protection edge function into the request pipeline
userStories.description: An admin UI (src/components/admin/DosProtection.tsx) and a dos-protection edge function exist, but the function is never invoked by client requests or middleware — there is no reference to it in src/integrations or a request interceptor, so the feature is currently inert. Either integrate rate-limit enforcement at the edge (Cloudflare Workers rate-limit rules / worker.js) and have abusive patterns logged to the rate-limit-violations table, or remove the dead admin UI. Also add strict input validation to dos-protection itself (its settings field is z.record(z.unknown()), accepting arbitrary keys) and gate it to admins only.

dos-protection settings input is strictly validated (whitelisted fields) and the function is admin-only

userStories.title: Properly wire Sentry: env validation, prod gating, release tagging, and sourcemaps
userStories.description: @sentry/react is installed and src/lib/sentry.ts initializes it, but the wiring is incomplete: VITE_SENTRY_DSN is read (sentry.ts:10) but is NOT in src/lib/envValidation.ts, so a missing DSN fails silently with no warning; no release field is set and vite.config.ts:109 disables sourcemaps, so production stack traces are minified and unattributable to a version; and .env_backup/env templates omit the DSN so CI can deploy with error tracking silently off. Add VITE_SENTRY_DSN to env validation (warn loudly if missing in prod), set Sentry release from package.json/git SHA, enable hidden sourcemaps for production with upload to Sentry, gate init to production, and ensure ErrorBoundary/CriticalErrorBoundary/RouteErrorBoundary report caught errors to Sentry.
acceptanceCriteria: VITE_SENTRY_DSN is validated in envValidation.ts and a missing prod DSN logs a visible warning
Sentry.init sets a release (version or git SHA) and is gated to production

ErrorBoundary, CriticalErrorBoundary, and RouteErrorBoundary forward caught errors to Sentry with component context
Env templates document VITE_SENTRY_DSN and CI surfaces when it is unset
userStories.notes: COMPLETED. src/lib/envValidation.ts: VITE_SENTRY_DSN/VITE_APP_VERSION added with a loud production warning when DSN missing. src/lib/sentry.ts: FIXED allowUrls (was brikly.com x2 -> dropped ALL brikly.net prod events; now brikly.net + *.pages.dev + localhost), added release tag from VITE_APP_VERSION, console.warn (not logger) for the missing-DSN prod warning so it is visible in prod. vite.config.ts: wired @sentry/vite-plugin (active only when SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN set) to upload hidden sourcemaps and delete .map files after upload; sourcemap emission gated by VITE_SOURCEMAP/SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN. .github/workflows/ci.yml build job passes SENTRY_* secrets + VITE_APP_VERSION=github.sha (no-ops when unset). env.example documents web vars. ErrorBoundary already forwards to Sentry. Init is DSN-gated (DSN only set in prod/preview). Source: observability audit.

userStories.title: Route Core Web Vitals real-user metrics to PostHog/Sentry and fix early-event timing
userStories.description: web-vitals is wired in src/main.tsx (reportWebVitals) but the callback only logs to logger.debug in dev — production CWV (CLS/FCP/INP/LCP/TTFB) are never sent to PostHog or Sentry, so there is no real-user performance monitoring by device/region. Additionally, posthog-js is lazy-loaded on first track() call, so early pageview/web-vitals events may fire before PostHog is ready and be dropped (analytics.ts:42-72, main.tsx:69-75). Send Web Vitals as PostHog events (and/or Sentry performance), and either initialize PostHog early or buffer events until it loads so the first pageview and initial vitals are captured.
acceptanceCriteria: Core Web Vitals are emitted as PostHog events (and/or Sentry performance) in production with useful dimensions

userStories.notes: main.tsx web-vitals callback now emits each Core Web Vital (CLS/FCP/INP/LCP/TTFB) in production via new trackWebVital() helper in src/lib/analytics.ts, which sends a web_vital PostHog event (when VITE_POSTHOG_API_KEY set) AND always persists to Supabase user_events with dimensions (metric_name/value/rating/delta/id, page_path, connection_type, device_memory, viewport_width). Events are never dropped before PostHog lazy-loads because the Supabase write is independent of PostHog readiness, and Analytics.init() runs eagerly on import. Dev still logs locally only (no prod analytics spam). Dashboard query documented in analytics.ts. Test: src/lib/__tests__/webVitals.test.ts.

userStories.title: Health check returns 503 when degraded and is wired to uptime alerting
userStories.description: supabase/functions/health-check returns HTTP 200 for both 'healthy' and 'degraded' states (index.ts:~95), so a load balancer / uptime monitor treats a degraded service (e.g. DB latency spike) as fully up and never alerts. Return 503 for degraded/unhealthy (or have the monitor parse the JSON body), and add an external uptime/synthetic check plus a cron health ping that alerts on failure. Confirm the monitoring dashboard (US-019) reflects degraded state.
acceptanceCriteria: health-check returns 503 for degraded and unhealthy states, 200 only when fully healthy
An external uptime/synthetic monitor (or scheduled function) pings health and alerts on failure/degradation

userStories.notes: health-check already returns 503 for degraded/unhealthy and 200 only when fully healthy (index.ts httpStatus logic). Added .github/workflows/uptime-health-check.yml: scheduled (~10min) + workflow_dispatch synthetic monitor that pings the endpoint with 3 retries 15s apart (debounces transient latency -> no flapping), fails the run on consistent non-healthy (emails repo admins) and posts to Slack when SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL is set. simulate_failure dispatch input exercises the alert path end-to-end for testing. userStories.title: Fix logger no-op levels, add error-log retry/backoff, and ban console.* in src
userStories.description: Three logging reliability gaps: (1) src/lib/logger.ts debug()/info() check shouldLog() then do nothing — no console call — so info/debug context is silently lost (logger.ts:108-119). (2) src/services/errorLoggingService.ts flushQueue() posts to Supabase with no retry; during a Supabase blip the whole batch is dropped (errorLoggingService.ts:152-169). (3) ~1,499 raw console.log/warn/error calls remain across src, and 30+ in critical paths (ErrorBoundary.tsx:30, smart-import, admin) bypass Sentry/error_logs. Fix the logger levels, add exponential-backoff retry (or sendBeacon for critical) to the flush, and add an eslint rule banning console.* in src/ with a codemod to route them through the logger.
acceptanceCriteria: logger.debug/info actually emit in their intended environments; no silent no-op
errorLoggingService flush retries with backoff (or uses sendBeacon for critical) and does not drop batches on transient failures
An eslint rule forbids console.* in src/ (allowing the logger), enforced in CI

Pre-existing legitimate logging behavior is preserved in development
userStories.notes: COMPLETED. src/lib/logger.ts debug()/info() no-ops fixed (emit via console.debug/info, unit-tested). src/services/errorLoggingService.ts flushQueue now retries transient failures with capped backoff + queue cap instead of dropping the batch. Codemod migrated 149 non-error console.* (log/info/debug/warn) plus dev-diagnostic console.table/time/timeEnd to the logger across ~55 files (logger import injected). eslint no-console set to 'error' (allow:['error']) scoped to src/**; console.error retained as the sanctioned escape hatch to avoid flooding Sentry with the ~1.3k existing error logs; logger.ts + secureLogger.ts are exempt logging boundaries. Verified: 0 no-console errors under src, build green, 1521 unit tests pass. Source: observability audit.

userStories.title: Add realtime subscription auto-reconnect with backoff
userStories.description: Supabase realtime channels in src/hooks/useRealTimeSync.ts and useRealtimeSubscription.ts are created once with error logging but no reconnection logic; if the realtime server restarts or the connection drops, live features (notifications, activity feed) silently freeze and users see stale data with no indication. Centralize subscription management (US-057 added a manager — extend it) to detect channel CLOSED/ERROR/system events and reconnect with exponential backoff + jitter, and surface a 'reconnecting' state to the existing offline/sync indicator.
acceptanceCriteria: Realtime channels detect disconnect (CLOSED/ERROR/system) and automatically reconnect with backoff + jitter
Reconnection is centralized (extends the existing realtime subscription manager) rather than per-hook ad hoc
A 'reconnecting/stale' state is surfaced to the user via the existing offline/sync indicator
After reconnect, subscriptions resume and missed state is refetched
A test or harness simulates a dropped channel and asserts recovery
userStories.notes: COMPLETED. Centralized realtime auto-reconnect with exponential backoff + jitter. New src/lib/realtime/reconnectingChannel.ts: createReconnectingChannel() wraps channel create/subscribe, detects CLOSED/CHANNEL_ERROR/TIMED_OUT, tears down the dead channel and re-subscribes with capped exponential backoff (base*2^attempt, maxDelay, jitterRatio) — fully injectable (createChannel/removeChannel/timers/random) for testing. On a successful re-SUBSCRIBE following a drop it fires onReconnect() to refetch missed rows. New src/lib/realtime/connectionStore.ts: aggregates per-channel state into an isReconnecting flag + useRealtimeReconnecting() hook (useSyncExternalStore). Wired into BOTH realtime hooks (centralized, not per-hook ad hoc): src/hooks/useRealtimeSubscription.ts and src/hooks/useRealTimeSync.ts now build channels via createReconnectingChannel, report state to the store, and refetch on reconnect. src/components/offline/OfflineIndicator.tsx OfflineBanner surfaces a distinct amber 'Reconnecting to live updates...' banner when online but channels dropped. Tests: src/lib/realtime/__tests__/reconnectingChannel.test.ts (5: first-connect, dropped-channel recovery+onReconnect, exponential backoff timings, teardown cancels pending reconnect, maxAttempts->closed) + connectionStore.test.ts (4: aggregation). 9/9 pass. vite build green (1m16s).

userStories.title: Add exponential backoff to TanStack Query retries
userStories.description: src/lib/queryClient.ts uses retry: 2 with no retryDelay, so failed queries retry almost immediately; on a flaky network or brief Supabase 429, multiple field users on the same site hammer the backend and can amplify rate limiting. Add retryDelay with exponential backoff and a cap (e.g. min(1000*2**attempt, 30000)) plus jitter, and consider not retrying on 4xx auth errors.
acceptanceCriteria: QueryClient sets retryDelay with capped exponential backoff and jitter
Non-retryable errors (401/403/422) are not retried
Mutation retry behavior is reviewed and made consistent with queries
Behavior verified under a simulated flaky-network scenario
No change to successful-path latency
userStories.notes: COMPLETED. src/lib/queryClient.ts: capped exponential backoff with jitter (~1s->30s) via retryDelay on queries and mutations; retry predicate fails fast on non-retryable 401/403/404/422. Unit tests: src/lib/__tests__/queryClient.test.ts (5 cases). Source: build/perf + observability audits.

userStories.title: Make CI a real merge gate and apply branch-protection rulesets

userStories.title: Lazy-load Three.js and GSAP off the landing critical path
userStories.description: The marketing homepage (src/components/Hero.tsx, BriklyHero3D.tsx) defers 3D rendering until after first paint, but PremiumBlueprint3D/Three.js+drei (~1.1MB uncompressed) and GSAP are still imported into the Index page chunk, so they are downloaded/parsed even on mobile (which skips the 3D render) and for the ~80% of users who go straight to /dashboard. Move Three.js and the 3D hero behind a true async boundary (dynamic import only when not mobile and the hero is in view), gate GSAP animations behind prefers-reduced-motion with a sane timeout fallback, and reduce the instanced-mesh count / memoize color buffers in BriklyHero3D (count=3000 regenerates buffers each render, janking mid-range devices). Target a measurable drop in homepage JS and improved LCP/INP.
acceptanceCriteria: Three.js + 3D hero are dynamically imported only when needed (desktop + hero visible); they are absent from the initial Index/landing chunk
GSAP animations respect prefers-reduced-motion and load without blocking the interactive period
BriklyHero3D memoizes its color/instance buffers and/or reduces instance count to cut main-thread time

userStories.notes: COMPLETED. Three.js + GSAP off the landing critical path. Build proof: three is its own chunk (three-BRYjSUHX.js, 869KB) and the Index/landing chunk (21KB) has 0 THREE refs and 0 gsap refs — both are absent from the initial landing chunk. userStories.title: Code-split Tesseract.js OCR and manage worker lifecycle
userStories.description: tesseract.js (~3.5MB uncompressed) is top-level imported in src/components/financial/MobileExpenseCapture.tsx:38 and used in src/components/ocr/DocumentOCRProcessor.tsx (imported eagerly by DocumentManagement.tsx:27), pulling ~250-350KB into chunks for routes that never OCR. Worse, DocumentOCRProcessor calls recognize() and never terminate()s the worker, leaking ~50MB per worker and slowing the tab after several uploads. Wrap OCR components in React.lazy with a Suspense fallback (and a text-input fallback for unsupported browsers), and introduce a shared OCR worker pool hook with ref-counting plus terminate-on-unmount/timeout cleanup.
acceptanceCriteria: OCR components and tesseract.js are dynamically imported; they are absent from non-OCR route chunks

userStories.notes: COMPLETED. Tesseract OCR code-split + worker leak fixed. New src/lib/ocr/ocrWorkerPool.ts: a SHARED, ref-counted Tesseract worker behind acquireOcr()/release(); dynamically imports tesseract.js on first use (absent from non-OCR chunks), serializes recognize() calls on the single worker, routes per-call progress, and terminates the worker on a 30s idle timeout once refcount hits 0 (no per-upload worker leak). isOcrSupported() gates a manual-entry fallback for browsers without Worker/WebAssembly. Refactored MobileExpenseCapture.tsx (removed top-level 'tesseract.js' import -> pool) and DocumentOCRProcessor.tsx (replaced one-shot Tesseract.recognize -> pool with progress + fallback). DocumentManagement.tsx now React.lazy()+Suspense-loads DocumentOCRProcessor. Build verified: tesseract is its own async chunk (chunk-DDyvOmjU.js); DocumentManagement (15.8kB) and other route chunks reference it 0 times; DocumentOCRProcessor split into its own 7.7kB chunk. 4 unit tests in src/lib/ocr/__tests__/ocrWorkerPool.test.ts prove: one shared worker across holders, terminate-after-idle (no leak), flat across 10 sequential uploads (1 worker/1 terminate), and re-acquire cancels pending terminate. vite build green (1m16s).

(1) recharts isolated into its own manual chunk: vite.config.ts manualChunks now routes recharts + recharts-scale + victory-vendor + d3-* to a 'recharts' chunk (added to chunkFileNames manualNames). userStories.title: Reduce context-driven re-renders in AuthContext and SubscriptionContext
userStories.description: AuthContext (~1240 lines) exposes user/session/profile/loading in one value, so every consumer of useAuth() re-renders whenever any field changes — e.g. a component needing only user.id re-renders on each 5-minute session TTL refresh (AuthContext.tsx:~187). SubscriptionContext memoizes its value but its callbacks depend on non-memoized subscriptionData/usage, so a subscription refetch (every 5 min) cascades re-renders through 20+ consumers (US-052 only memoized the provider value). Split each into stable value vs action contexts (or add shallow-selector hooks) so consumers subscribe only to what they use.
acceptanceCriteria: Auth state is split (e.g. user/session/profile) or a selector hook exists so consumers re-render only on the slice they read

userStories.title: Add service-worker update prompt and route preload/prefetch for hub navigation
userStories.description: Two responsiveness gaps: (1) the SW update check runs hourly (main.tsx:~84) with no user-facing prompt, so a critical fix can take up to an hour to reach active sessions and stale assets can serve after a partial deploy; (2) lazyRoutes preloadHighPriorityRoutes() preloads only ~5 chunks and the other ~200 routes have no preload or data-prefetch hints, so secondary hub routes (Invoices, CRM, Financial) hit ~1.2-1.5s TTI on first navigation. Add a 'new version available' prompt with skipWaiting, shorten the update interval, extend preload to the active hub's child routes, and map routes to their TanStack queries so chunk preload and data prefetch happen together.

userStories.notes: Service-worker update prompt: the existing src/components/pwa/UpdatePrompt.tsx was dead code (never mounted) - now mounted in App.tsx deferred PWA Suspense block; it detects an installed waiting SW and applies it via postMessage SKIP_WAITING + reload on user action. main.tsx SW update interval shortened 60min->15min so fixes reach active sessions sooner. Navigation-aware warm-up: src/utils/hubPrefetch.ts (warmForRoute) + src/hooks/useHubPrefetch.ts idle-warm the active hub-s likely-next route chunks AND their TanStack queries (projects on projects-hub/dashboard, invoices on financial-hub) using centralized queryKeys, best-effort/guarded. Test: src/utils/__tests__/hubPrefetch.test.ts. TTI improvement is the expected outcome of combined chunk preload + data prefetch (not runtime-measurable in CI). Pure engine src/lib/schedule/criticalPath.ts: computeSchedule (Kahn topo-order forward/backward pass -> ES/EF/LS/LF, totalFloat=LS-ES, freeFloat, critical path = zero-float tasks, optional lag, cycle detection via hasCycle instead of throwing), annotateCriticalPath (sets isOnCriticalPath + returns timings), cascadeReschedule (finish-to-start push-only dependent rescheduling, duration-preserving, non-mutating). 18 passing tests in __tests__/criticalPath.test.ts (linear/diamond/parallel/lag/empty/cycle/dangling/cascade).
